title: fix(plugin-security): an assignment write the administrator cannot address answers not-found, as a read does; a refusal names only values the caller can read
body:
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：组织管理员和委派管理员按 id 修改或删除授权行（`sys_user_position`、`sys_user_permission_set`）时，如果这一行自己读不到，或这个 id 根本没有对应的行，现在都回答读取门的 `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND`，和读取这个 id、以及其他任何对象按 id 写入时的回答完全一样。委派管理员被拒时，提示和 details 里只出现调用者自己读得到、或自己写进去的值。
- 为什么改：落实维护者裁决：按 id 写入时，读不到的行按读取门的回答处理；拒绝提示不写出调用者读不到的字段值，判定照旧按存储行做。
- 风险与回滚：只是同一类拒绝的状态码从 403 换成 404，原来放行的写入一律照旧放行；读得到的行判定和提示不变；插入、租户级管理员、读取被整体拒绝的调用者都不受影响。回滚即撤销本 PR。
- 先看：`security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts` 里 `readDoorAnswerForGateRefusal` 新增的 not-found 分支；`delegated-admin-gate.ts` 里的 `UnreadableAddressedRowRefusal`、`delegatedTargets` 和 `mayName`；组织管理员分支 `organizationAdminFailure` 对 update 先问一次读取。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security exec vitest run src/org-admin-assignment-boundary.posture.test.ts`，预期 74/74 通过。
- 需要你做的：确认本 PR 对两条未发布 changeset 的改写（见 Acceptance notes 第一条）；`check-empty-changeset` 在你确认之前按设计保持红。

## What changes

- **An assignment write the administrator cannot address answers not-found, as a read does.** For the by-id update or delete the caller addressed, when the delegated-administration gate (ADR-0090 D12) refused it because the caller's own read of the row returned none, the security middleware now answers `recordNotFoundError` for that object and id: the read door's `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND`, which step 2.7 already answers for every other object. This covers the organization administrator's branch and the delegated branch (a delegate holding an `adminScope`, and an organization administrator who holds one too). A row the caller cannot read and an id naming no row get the same answer, and it is the same answer a `GET` of that id gets.
  - The gate marks that refusal with its own class, `UnreadableAddressedRowRefusal` (a `PermissionDeniedError`). Only `readDoorAnswerForGateRefusal` turns it into the not-found, and only for the by-id write the caller addressed (`addressedByIdWriteId`, with step 2.7's exclusions). A nested write, a referential clear and the write-admission preview keep the gate's `403`, which names no row and no id.
  - A caller the read door refuses outright still gets that read refusal, unchanged.
  - An organization administrator's edit in place is asked the read question first, so an edit of a row it reads is still refused as an edit (`403`).
- **A refusal names a value only when the caller can read it.** In the delegated walk, each value its guidance names — the position, the sets it distributes, the business unit, the holder, the permission set — is named only when the caller wrote it (an insert's row, a column its update payload carries), or when the caller's own read of the row returned that column at its stored value (`mayName`). Otherwise the sentence is the same without the value, for example "the assignment's position distributes a permission set which is not in the scope's allowlist", and `details` leaves the value out. The verdict does not change: it is still taken on the stored row.
  - "Can read" is the read door's own answer, not a second evaluator. The gate already holds the caller's read of the row (`readAsCaller`, the operation's memoised pre-image read). A column a field rule hides is absent from that read, and a masked column differs from the stored value, so neither is named.
  - The organization administrator's branch already words its refusal of a removal from the caller's own read, so it names nothing that read hides. It is pinned here and not changed.
- **Two unreleased changesets corrected.** `.changeset/org-admin-removal-caller-read.md` and `.changeset/delegated-admin-unreadable-row.md` said the answer is `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`. This change makes that false, so each now names the not-found.

## Tests

- `org-admin-assignment-boundary.posture.test.ts` (real ObjectQL engine and SQL driver, real `SecurityPlugin`):
  - Under `group` and `isolated`, for both tables, both verbs, and a row the caller cannot read as well as an id naming no row:
    - the organization administrator (both sets), the delegate and the organization administrator who holds a scope each answer the read door's not-found, compared whole (status, code, name, message, every own field) with `recordNotFoundError` for that id;
    - the tenant-level administrator, whom step 2.7 answers, gets the same whole answer;
    - a delegate the read door refuses gets that read refusal, whole.
  - In every posture, for each of the four columns a refusal could name, a delegate whose field rules hide the column is refused `DELEGATION_SCOPE_VIOLATION`, and its value appears nowhere in the answer. The delegate who reads the column gets the same verdict, with the value named. A value the caller wrote is named. An organization administrator whose field rules hide the column is refused without the value.
  - A partially masked column (a masking rule on `position`, not `readable: false`): the delegate reads the masked value, and neither that value nor the stored one appears anywhere in the serialized refusal. The verdict still comes from the stored row: refused for a stored position off the allowlist, admitted for one inside the scope.
  - The field-hidden-position control from the delegated describe is re-pinned to the verdict and code, plus no hidden value in the answer.
  - Controls kept: in-scope rows the caller reads are admitted; out-of-scope rows it reads keep their guidance with the values; the tenant-level administrator is answered as before; in `single`, rows the caller reads keep their guidance and an id naming no row answers the not-found.
- HTTP dogfood (showcase, `isolated`): `org-admin-assignment-removal-unreadable-row` and `delegated-admin-assignment-write-unreadable-row` now pin `PATCH` and `DELETE`, of the row and of an id naming none, to equal exactly what a `GET` of that id answers (`404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND`, status and body). Each has a measured red leg, below.

## Acceptance notes

- **Correcting two pending release notes: please confirm.** This PR rewrites the first bullet of `.changeset/org-admin-removal-caller-read.md` and of `.changeset/delegated-admin-unreadable-row.md`. Neither has shipped (the plugin's `CHANGELOG.md` holds neither, and npm has `18.3.0`). Both said a row the caller cannot read answers `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, which this change makes false. Each now says the read door's `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND`. `check-empty-changeset` names both files and stays red by design until a maintainer confirms. Restoring them from the base would republish the false sentence.
- The Setup screens that remove an assignment (Assigned users on a permission set, Position holders on a position) show the server's sentence for any refused removal, whatever the status, and fall back to their localized "Failed to remove" line. Nothing under `ui/` treats a `403` and a `404` from these writes differently. They list only rows the caller reads, so the new answer reaches them only when a row was removed in between. That answer now reads "Record … not found in …" where it used to read as an access refusal.
- A caller with no administrator authority over these tables is answered as before.
